                "+<p dir=\"auto\">After a merge, Hive Mind now checks every issue the pull request is meant to close and closes the ones GitHub left open, for example after a merge into a branch other than the default one (issues <a class=\"issue-link js-issue-link\" data-error-text=\"Failed to load title\" data-id=\"5867555563\" data-permission-text=\"Title is private\" data-url=\"https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/issues/3354\" data-hovercard-type=\"issue\" data-hovercard-url=\"/link-assistant/hive-mind/issues/3354/hovercard\" href=\"https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/issues/3354\">#3354</a>, <a class=\"issue-link js-issue-link\" data-error-text=\"Failed to load title\" data-id=\"5867556892\" data-permission-text=\"Title is private\" data-url=\"https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/issues/3355\" data-hovercard-type=\"issue\" data-hovercard-url=\"/link-assistant/hive-mind/issues/3355/hovercard\" href=\"https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/issues/3355\">#3355</a> and <a class=\"issue-link js-issue-link\" data-error-text=\"Failed to load title\" data-id=\"5867559550\" data-permission-text=\"Title is private\" data-url=\"https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/issues/3357\" data-hovercard-type=\"issue\" data-hovercard-url=\"/link-assistant/hive-mind/issues/3357/hovercard\" href=\"https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/issues/3357\">#3357</a>). It waits up to 5 minutes (checks after 10, 20, 40 and 60 seconds) for GitHub on a default-branch merge, then closes each remaining issue as completed with a comment that names the pull request, the merge commit and why GitHub did not close it. The result appears in the log, in the auto-merge comment and in the Telegram merge queue message. Issues the description keeps open (\"does not close\", \"Part of\"), issues only a repair block or a sidebar link names, and deferred sub-issues are never closed. This is on by default; <code class=\"notranslate\">--no-auto-close-linked-issues</code> or <code class=\"notranslate\">HIVE_MIND_AUTO_CLOSE_LINKED_ISSUES=false</code> only reports the open issues. <code class=\"notranslate\">/merge</code>, solve's auto-merge, the merge queue, the merged-PR sweeper and <code class=\"notranslate\">close-linked-issues</code> now share this one implementation, which replaces the previous per-path closing code.</p>",
                "+<p dir=\"auto\">Pull requests merged outside Hive Mind (the GitHub UI, a person's <code class=\"notranslate\">gh pr merge</code>, GitHub auto-merge) now get their intended issues closed too (issue <a class=\"issue-link js-issue-link\" data-error-text=\"Failed to load title\" data-id=\"5867558330\" data-permission-text=\"Title is private\" data-url=\"https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/issues/3356\" data-hovercard-type=\"issue\" data-hovercard-url=\"/link-assistant/hive-mind/issues/3356/hovercard\" href=\"https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/issues/3356\">#3356</a>). The Telegram bot (your own pull requests) and hive (the monitored repository or owner) run a sweeper every 5 minutes over pull requests merged in the last 24 hours. It skips ones merged in the last 5 minutes, checks each one only once, and stores its cursor in <code class=\"notranslate\">~/.hive-mind/merged-pr-sweeper.json</code> (or <code class=\"notranslate\">HIVE_MIND_MERGED_PR_SWEEPER_STATE</code>). It never touches pull requests merged before it was first enabled. The new <code class=\"notranslate\">close-linked-issues --pr &lt;url&gt; [--dry-run]</code> command does the same for one pull request and prints what it would close and what it skips and why. <code class=\"notranslate\">close-linked-issues --repo &lt;owner/repo&gt; --since &lt;date&gt;</code> (or <code class=\"notranslate\">--owner</code>) backfills older merges.</p>",
                "+<p dir=\"auto\">A closing reference to an issue in another repository that the pull request author wrote in the description (above any repair block) no longer blocks the merge, and the issue is closed explicitly after the merge, because GitHub does not close it (issue <a class=\"issue-link js-issue-link\" data-error-text=\"Failed to load title\" data-id=\"5867560819\" data-permission-text=\"Title is private\" data-url=\"https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/issues/3358\" data-hovercard-type=\"issue\" data-hovercard-url=\"/link-assistant/hive-mind/issues/3358/hovercard\" href=\"https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/issues/3358\">#3358</a>). Foreign references that the link repair appended, or that come from a sub-issue tree, still block the merge, as in issue <a class=\"issue-link js-issue-link\" data-error-text=\"Failed to load title\" data-id=\"5852684068\" data-permission-text=\"Title is private\" data-url=\"https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/issues/3276\" data-hovercard-type=\"issue\" data-hovercard-url=\"/link-assistant/hive-mind/issues/3276/hovercard\" href=\"https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/issues/3276\">#3276</a>. A sidebar-only foreign link still blocks it too. <code class=\"notranslate\">--no-allow-cross-repository-closing</code> or <code class=\"notranslate\">HIVE_MIND_ALLOW_CROSS_REPOSITORY_CLOSING=false</code> restores the previous rule, which blocks every foreign closing reference.</p>",
                "+<p dir=\"auto\">After the post-merge check closes an issue, Hive Mind now walks up its parent issues and closes each one whose work is complete (issue <a class=\"issue-link js-issue-link\" data-error-text=\"Failed to load title\" data-id=\"5867561955\" data-permission-text=\"Title is private\" data-url=\"https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/issues/3359\" data-hovercard-type=\"issue\" data-hovercard-url=\"/link-assistant/hive-mind/issues/3359/hovercard\" href=\"https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/issues/3359\">#3359</a>). A parent is closed only when four things hold. First, every sub-issue is closed as completed; one closed as not planned or as a duplicate counts only if the parent description says so. Second, the description has no unchecked ta[REDACTED] item and no open \"Done when\" item. Third, nothing blocks it. Fourth, nobody reopened it after its last sub-issue closed. Otherwise, the parent gets one status comment with the reasons, which is updated instead of repeated. Sub-issues are never closed because their parent closed. This is on by default; turn it off with <code class=\"notranslate\">--no-close-completed-parents</code> or <code class=\"notranslate\">HIVE_MIND_CLOSE_COMPLETED_PARENTS=false</code>.</p>",
                "+<p dir=\"auto\">Dependencies are current, and CI demands it everywhere a version is declared (issue <a class=\"issue-link js-issue-link\" data-error-text=\"Failed to load title\" data-id=\"5852840606\" data-permission-text=\"Title is private\" data-url=\"https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/issues/3282\" data-hovercard-type=\"issue\" data-hovercard-url=\"/link-assistant/hive-mind/issues/3282/hovercard\" href=\"https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/issues/3282\">#3282</a>). The freshness gate now also checks transitive <code class=\"notranslate\">package-lock.json</code> entries that <code class=\"notranslate\">npm update</code> would move, images held in Dockerfile <code class=\"notranslate\">ARG</code>s or pinned by digest, image references in source code, the coolify Dockerfile and the example workflows users copy. It ignores prose and commented-out lines, and reads every page of a registry's tags. A hold on an older version must name its open follow-up issue, such as link-assistant/router 0.x (<a class=\"issue-link js-issue-link\" data-error-text=\"Failed to load title\" data-id=\"5880066090\" data-permission-text=\"Title is private\" data-url=\"https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/issues/3395\" data-hovercard-type=\"issue\" data-hovercard-url=\"/link-assistant/hive-mind/issues/3395/hovercard\" href=\"https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/issues/3395\">#3395</a>). Formal AI stays just another model: <code class=\"notranslate\">hive</code> and <code class=\"notranslate\">solve</code> also stop an unleased Formal AI sidecar and unload an image unused past <code class=\"notranslate\">HIVE_MIND_FORMAL_AI_UNLOAD_AFTER</code>, not only the Telegram bot, and a host that never ran Formal AI makes no Docker call for it. Model validation and the runtime share one list of the tools Formal AI runs through. The Telegram bot treats a command argument as a GitHub URL only when it names the github.com host, and the merge queue's MarkdownV2 escaping covers backslashes, also in its CI run links. Claude Code now receives the system prompt, and a resumed session's prompt, exactly as written. Before, every <code class=\"notranslate\">\"</code> in them arrived as <code class=\"notranslate\">\\\"</code>, and with command-stream 0.18.0 /bin/sh expanded their <code class=\"notranslate\">$(...)</code> and backticks: every run logged <code class=\"notranslate\">/bin/sh: 1: .png: not found</code>. The body is now sent as JSON on stdin (`--input -`), so the `\\n` and quote workarounds only damage correct text.\n\n## Impact\n\nFound while fixing link-assistant/hive-mind#3445: the [v2.37.1 release](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/releases/tag/v2.37.1) of hive-mind rendered one bullet followed by 18 loose paragraphs. An audit of all 893 hive-mind releases found 302 with lost indentation, 21 more with missing text and 37 never formatted. Example in this template's own downstream: [link-foundation/start v0.13.0](https://github.com/link-foundation/start/releases/tag/v0.13.0) lost the `- 7763ae1:` bullet and the indentation of its nested list (compare with its CHANGELOG.md section).\n\nCopies of the same code (found with `gh search code \"line.trim()) // Trim whitespace from each line\"`):\n\n- link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template `scripts/format-release-notes.mjs`\n- link-foundation/command-stream `js/scripts/format-release-notes.mjs`\n- link-foundation/gh-load-issue, link-foundation/gh-load-pull-request, link-foundation/glab-setup-git-identity, link-foundation/pdf-to-markdown, link-foundation/start, link-foundation/test-anywhere `scripts/format-release-notes.mjs`\n- link-foundation/lino-objects-codec `js/scripts/format-release-notes.mjs`\n- link-assistant/agent, link-assistant/meta-expression, link-assistant/web-capture `scripts/format-release-notes.mjs`, link-assistant/web-search `js/scripts/format-release-notes.mjs`\n\n## Reproduction\n\n```js\n// node repro.mjs: the cleanup step of scripts/format-release-notes.mjs (lines 145-156)\nconst body = `### Patch Changes\n\n- 68f606a: First change.\n\n  Second change of the same changeset.\n\n  - nested bullet\n  - another nested bullet\n\n  ---\n\n  Text after a rule, and a literal \\`\\\\n\\` in code. Ends with a \"quote\"`;\n\nconst changesPattern = /### (Major|Minor|Patch) Changes\\s*\\n\\s*-\\s+(?:([a-f0-9]+):\\s+)?(.+?)$/s;\nconst [, , , rawDescription] = body.match(changesPattern);\nconst cleanDescription = rawDescription\n  .replace(/\\\\n/g, '\\n')\n  .replace(/^(\\\\['\"])+/g, '')\n  .replace(/(['\"])+$/g, '')\n  .replace(/^(['\"])+/g, '')\n  .replace(/📦.*$/s, '')\n  .replace(/---.*$/s, '')\n  .trim()\n  .split('\\n')\n  .map((line) => line.trim())\n  .join('\\n')\n  .replace(/\\n{3,}/g, '\\n\\n');\nconsole.log(cleanDescription);\n```\n\nActual output: the bullet and hash are gone, the second paragraph and the nested list are no longer inside the item, and everything from `---` on is lost:\n\n```\nFirst change.\n\nSecond change of the same changeset.\n\n- nested bullet\n- another nested bullet\n```\n\nExpected: the section exactly as changesets wrote it (only trailing whitespace removed).\n\n## Workaround\n\nFix a published release by rewriting its body from the CHANGELOG.md section, for example `gh api repos/OWNER/REPO/releases/ID -X PATCH --input body.json`. hive-mind ships [`scripts/repair-release-notes.mjs`](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/pull/3446) for this; it rebuilds every affected release (dry run by default).\n\n## Suggested fix\n\nKeep the structure and strip only what the formatter itself adds. This is the change made in link-assistant/hive-mind#3446 (`scripts/format-release-notes.lib.mjs`):\n\n```js\nconst CHANGE_SECTION = /^### (Major|Minor|Patch) Changes[ \\t]*$/gm;\n\nconst normalizeMarkdown = (text) =>\n  String(text || '')\n    .replace(/\\r\\n?/g, '\\n')\n    .split('\\n')\n    .map((line) => line.replace(/[ \\t]+$/, '')) // trailing whitespace only\n    .join('\\n')\n    .replace(/\\n{3,}/g, '\\n\\n')\n    .replace(/^\\n+/, '')\n    .replace(/\\s+$/, '');\n\nfunction buildReleaseDescription(body) {\n  const text = String(body || '').replace(/\\r\\n?/g, '\\n');\n  const headings = [...text.matchAll(CHANGE_SECTION)];\n  const sections = headings\n    .map((match, i) => ({\n      type: match[1],\n      content: normalizeMarkdown(text.slice(match.index + match[0].length, headings[i + 1]?.index ?? text.length)),\n    }))\n    .filter((section) => section.content);\n  const commitHashes = [...text.matchAll(/^[ \\t]*[-*][ \\t]+([a-f0-9]{7,40}):/gm)].map((m) => m[1]);\n  if (sections.length === 0) return { description: normalizeMarkdown(text), commitHashes };\n  if (sections.length === 1) return { description: sections[0].content, commitHashes };\n  return {\n    description: sections.map((s) => `### ${s.type} Changes\\n\\n${s.content}`).join('\\n\\n'),\n    commitHashes,\n  };\n}\n```\n\nAlso:\n\n- Drop the `\\n` and quote replacements; the body is sent as JSON on stdin.\n- Look up the PRs of every hash in `commitHashes`, not only the first.\n- In `create-github-release.mjs`, match the version heading as a whole line (`^## 1.2.3[ \\t]*$`) so `1.2.3` never reads the `1.2.30` section.\n\nTests that cover these cases are in [`tests/issue-3445-release-notes-formatting.test.mjs`](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/pull/3446).\nEOF\ngh issue list --repo link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template --search \"release notes indentation\" --state all --limit 5"
    }
  }

    "originalFile": "/**\n * Pure helpers behind the GitHub release notes of every published version.\n *\n * Why this exists (issue #3445):\n *   The release body is the CHANGELOG.md section of the version. A changeset\n *   with several paragraphs or a nested list becomes one list item whose\n *   continuation lines are indented by two spaces:\n *\n *     - 68f606a: First paragraph.\n *\n *       Second paragraph, still part of the item.\n *\n *   `format-release-notes.mjs` used to trim every line, so the second paragraph\n *   lost its indentation and rendered outside the list (v2.37.1), and nested\n *   bullets became siblings of their parent item. It also cut the notes at the\n *   first `---` or `###` anywhere in the text, rewrote a literal `\\n` inside a\n *   code span into a line break, stripped quotes the text ends with, and kept\n *   only one of the `### Minor Changes` / `### Patch Changes` sections.\n *\n *   These helpers keep the Markdown structure exactly as changesets wrote it:\n *   only trailing whitespace is removed, sections are found by headings at the\n *   start of a line, and only a footer this formatter generated is stripped.\n *\n * Uses only Node built-ins so it can be unit tested without the network.\n *\n * @see https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/issues/3445\n */\n\nexport const PACKAGE_NAME = '@link-assistant/hive-mind';\n\n// The section headings changesets writes, at the start of a line only. A `###`\n// inside a changeset's own text is indented under its list item, so it never\n// matches.\nconst CHANGE_SECTION_PATTERN = /^### (Major|Minor|Patch) Changes[ \\t]*$/gm;\n\n// The footer `buildReleaseBody` appends: a `---` rule followed by the npm badge.\nconst GENERATED_FOOTER_PATTERN = /\\n?^---[ \\t]*\\n(?:\\s*\\n)*\\s*(?:\\[!\\[npm version\\]\\(https:\\/\\/img\\.shields\\.io\\/badge\\/npm-|📦)[\\s\\S]*$/m;\nconst GENERATED_PR_LINE_PATTERN = /\\n?^\\*\\*Related Pull Requests?:\\*\\*[^\\n]*$/m;\nconst GENERATED_BADGE_PATTERN = /\\[!\\[npm version\\]\\(https:\\/\\/img\\.shields\\.io\\/badge\\/npm-/;\n\n/**\n * Escape a string for use inside a RegExp.\n * @param {string} value\n * @returns {string}\n */\nexport const escapeRegExp = value => value.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\\]\\\\]/g, '\\\\$&');\n\n/**\n * Whether a release body already carries the footer this formatter adds. Its `getReleaseLine` is\n(`node_modules/@changesets/changelog-git/dist/index.mjs`):\n\n```js\nconst [firstLine, ...futureLines] = changeset.summary.split('\\n').map(l => l.trimEnd());\nlet returnVal = `- ${changeset.commit ? `${changeset.commit.slice(0, 7)}: ` : ''}${firstLine}`;\nif (futureLines.length > 0) returnVal += `\\n${futureLines.map(l => `  ${l}`).join('\\n')}`;\n```\n\nSo a changeset becomes **one** list item, and every later line is indented by\ntwo spaces. CommonMark keeps a later block inside the list item only when it is\nindented to the item's content column, which is two columns for `- `\n([CommonMark 0.31.2, §5.2 List items](https://spec.commonmark.org/0.31.2/#list-items):\n\"indenting subsequent lines of Ls by W + N spaces, is a list item with Bs as its\ncontents\"). Remove the indentation and the paragraph ends the list.\n\n`changesets/action` creates GitHub releases by copying the `CHANGELOG.md`\nsection unchanged (`createRelease` in\n[`src/run.ts`](https://github.com/changesets/action/blob/main/src/run.ts) uses\n`body: changelogEntry.content`). The structure is only lost because this\nrepository rewrites the body afterwards.\n\n## Root causes\n\n### RC1 – every line was trimmed (lost indentation, 302 releases, including v2.37.1)\n\n`format-release-notes.mjs` cleaned the description with:\n\n```js\n.split('\\n')\n.map(line => line.trim()) // Trim whitespace from each line\n.join('\\n')\n```\n\nThe comment describes the intent (\"normalize whitespace\"), but for Markdown the\nleading whitespace is structure. Each continuation paragraph and nested list\nitem lost its two spaces. GitHub then closed the list after the first paragraph,\nwhich is exactly what v2.37.1 shows (`render/v2.37.1-before.html`):\n\n| Render of v2.37.1                      | Before | After |\n| -------------------------------------- | ------ | ----- |\n| `<li>` elements                        | 1      | 1     |\n| `<p>` inside the list item             | 0      | 19    |\n| `<p>` after the list                   | 20     | 2     |\n\n(The two paragraphs after the list in the repaired body are the\n`**Related Pull Request:** #3390` line and the npm badge, as before.)\n\nWhy it became visible now: `validate-changeset.mjs` allows exactly one\nchangeset per PR. PR #3390 shipped many changes, so its changeset had 19\nparagraphs. Earlier releases had the same bug, but with one or two paragraphs it\nwas easy to miss.\n\n### RC2 – text was dropped (102 releases)\n\n`data/missing-text-causes.txt` classifies every release whose body misses words\nof its `CHANGELOG.md` section:\n\n| Cause                                                                                                                       | Releases | Examples                          |\n| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- | --------------------------------- |\n| The regex `/### Patch Changes\\s*\\n\\s*-\\s+([a-f0-9]+):\\s+(.+?)$/s` consumed the first `- <hash>:` (used before #1271)          | 89       | v1.21.3, v1.17.2, v1.0.1          |\n| `CHANGELOG.md` has more list items than the release, e.g. two `## 1.48.1` version commits (`977129778`, `8ae1de446`) later merged into one section | 37       | v1.48.1, v1.46.8, v1.21.2         |\n| Only the first `### … Changes` section was kept (`(?=###\\|$)`), so a Minor release lost its Patch section, and so on        | 4        | v0.44.0, v0.46.0, v0.48.0, v1.4.0 |\n| Trailing quotes were stripped by `.replace(/(['\"])+$/g, '')`                                                                 | 3        | v1.20.1, v1.38.3, v1.49.3         |\n| A literal `\\n` in a code span became a                                                                 | 2        | v2.33.5, v2.33.6                  |\n| The body differs in other ways (the CHANGELOG text was edited after the release)                                            | 4        | v1.0.1, v1.21.4, v1.22.5, v1.23.7 |\n\nA release can have several causes, so the counts add up to more than 102.\n`.replace(/---.*$/s, '')` (cut at After #1271 it also\nmatched `### Minor Changes`, but never `### Major Changes`. When nothing matched\nit exited with \"Could not parse\" and the release kept the raw CHANGELOG text,\nwith no PR link and no npm badge (v0.39.0 … v1.22.0, and v2.0.0).\n\n### RC4 – the publication sanitizer masked code (v2.33.5, v2.33.6, plus four latent cases)\n\nThe release body goes through `sanitizeForPublication`. Its rules treated these\nas credentials:\n\n- `…Tokens: [REDACTED] and `token => [REDACTED] the value was `false` followed by a\n  closing backtick, or `…`.\n- `KNO…ARS`: the all-caps vendor-token pattern matched an\n  identifier without a digit.\n- `--tokens-budget-stats [REDACTED] and `--max-tokens [REDACTED] the CLI-credential rule\n  matched any `--…tokens…` option.\n- `…=<tokens>`: a placeholder was treated as a value.\n\nThe live releases contained only the first two cases. Both indent continuation lines by two spaces,\n  as quoted above.\n- **changesets/action** with `createGithubReleases: true` publishes the\n  CHANGELOG section unchanged. It uses a regex over `#` headings (it skips code\n  fences) to find the section, and ends it at the next heading of the same depth\n  ([`src/utils.ts`](https://github.com/changesets/action/blob/main/src/utils.ts)).\n  That is the approach `extractChangelogSection` now follows: whole heading\n  lines, and no rewriting of the content.\n- **semantic-release** (`@semantic-release/release-notes-generator`) and\n  **release-please** generate notes from Conventional Commit subjects, so they\n  avoid the problem by never reformatting user-written Markdown. Switching\n  release tools is out of scope. The useful lesson is the same: treat\n  CHANGELOG Markdown as opaque and only append to it.\n- **GitHub's generate-notes API** (`POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/releases/generate-notes`)\n  lists merged PRs. It could replace the PR lookup, but it does not use the\n  changeset text.\n- **CommonMark**: §5.2 (\"List items\") defines when a block stays inside a list\n  item. GitHub's `/markdown` API (GFM) was used to check the renders in\n  `render/`.\n\n## Upstream report\n\n`format-release-notes.mjs` came from\n[link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template](https://github.com/link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template).\nThe current template copy still has `.map((line) => line.trim())`, the `---`\ntruncation, `\\n` conversion, quote stripping, the first `- <hash>:` being\nconsumed, and a lookup of only the first hash. It was reported in\n[link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template#236](https://github.com/link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/issues/236).\nThe report includes a runnable reproduction, real broken output\n(link-foundation/start v0.13.0), a workaround and the suggested code. It also\nlists the repositories that carry a copy, so that they can be fixed from one\nplace:\n\n- link-foundation: command-stream, gh-load-issue, gh-load-pull-request,\n  glab-setup-git-identity, pdf-to-markdown, start, test-anywhere and\n  lino-objects-codec;\n- link-assistant: agent, meta-expression, web-capture and web-search.\n\n## Decisions and assumptions\n\n- **What \"nicely formatted\" means for v2.37.1.** One changeset is one list item\n  in `CHANGELOG.md`, and that is how GitHub renders the CHANGELOG. The release\n  now renders the same way: one bullet whose 19 paragraphs are indented inside\n  it. Splitting it into 19 bullets would make the release differ from the\n  CHANGELOG, and it would need the changeset to be rewritten.\n- **Source of truth.** Releases were rebuilt from the current `CHANGELOG.md`. So\n  where the CHANGELOG was edited after a release (for example the merged\n  `## 1.48.1` sections), the release now shows the current text.\n- **PR links** already present in a release were kept. A release without a PR\n  line (the unformatted ones) gets its PRs from its commit hashes, as the\n  formatter does.\n- Editing a release has no side effects here: no workflow is triggered by\n  `release` events. The original bodies are backed up in\n  `data/all-releases.json`.\n\n## How to reproduce and verify\n\n```bash\n# Regression tests (default suite)\nnode tests/issue-3445-release-notes-formatting.test.mjs\nnode tests/issue-3445-release-notes-not-masked.test.mjs\nnode tests/test-format-release-notes-1271.mjs\n\n# Audit any set of releases against CHANGELOG.md\ngh api repos/link-assistant/hive-mind/releases --paginate --jq '[.[] | {id, tag_name, published_at, body}]' | jq -s add > /tmp/releases.json\nnode experiments/issue-3445-audit-releases.mjs /tmp/releases.json > /tmp/audit.tsv\n\n# Plan a repair (dry run) and apply it\nnode scripts/repair-release-notes.mjs --verbose\nnode scripts/repair-release-notes.mjs --tag v2.37.1 --apply --backup-dir /tmp/release-backups\n```\n"

Its `getReleaseLine` is\n(`node_modules/@changesets/changelog-git/dist/index.mjs`):\n\n```js\nconst [firstLine, ...futureLines] = changeset.summary.split('\\n').map(l => l.trimEnd());\nlet returnVal = `- ${changeset.commit ? `${changeset.commit.slice(0, 7)}: ` : ''}${firstLine}`;\nif (futureLines.length > 0) returnVal += `\\n${futureLines.map(l => `  ${l}`).join('\\n')}`;\n```\n\nSo a changeset becomes **one** list item, and every later line is indented by\ntwo spaces. CommonMark keeps a later block inside the list item only when it is\nindented to the item's content column, which is two columns for `- `\n([CommonMark 0.31.2, §5.2 List items](https://spec.commonmark.org/0.31.2/#list-items):\n\"indenting subsequent lines of Ls by W + N spaces, is a list item with Bs as its\ncontents\"). Remove the indentation and the paragraph ends the list.\n\n`changesets/action` creates GitHub releases by copying the `CHANGELOG.md`\nsection unchanged (`createRelease` in\n[`src/run.ts`](https://github.com/changesets/action/blob/main/src/run.ts) uses\n`body: changelogEntry.content`). The structure is only lost because this\nrepository rewrites the body afterwards.\n\n## Root causes\n\n### RC1 – every line was trimmed (lost indentation, 302 releases, including v2.37.1)\n\n`format-release-notes.mjs` cleaned the description with:\n\n```js\n.split('\\n')\n.map(line => line.trim()) // Trim whitespace from each line\n.join('\\n')\n```\n\nThe comment describes the intent (\"normalize whitespace\"), but for Markdown the\nleading whitespace is structure. Each continuation paragraph and nested list\nitem lost its two spaces. GitHub then closed the list after the first paragraph,\nwhich is exactly what v2.37.1 shows (`render/v2.37.1-before.html`):\n\n| Render of v2.37.1                      | Before | After |\n| -------------------------------------- | ------ | ----- |\n| `<li>` elements                        | 1      | 1     |\n| `<p>` inside the list item             | 0      | 19    |\n| `<p>` after the list                   | 20     | 2     |\n\n(The two paragraphs after the list in the repaired body are the\n`**Related Pull Request:** #3390` line and the npm badge, as before.)\n\nWhy it became visible now: `validate-changeset.mjs` allows exactly one\nchangeset per PR. PR #3390 shipped many changes, so its changeset had 19\nparagraphs. Earlier releases had the same bug, but with one or two paragraphs it\nwas easy to miss.\n\n### RC2 – text was dropped (102 releases)\n\n`data/missing-text-causes.txt` classifies every release whose body misses words\nof its `CHANGELOG.md` section:\n\n| Cause                                                                                                                       | Releases | Examples                          |\n| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- | --------------------------------- |\n| The regex `/### Patch Changes\\s*\\n\\s*-\\s+([a-f0-9]+):\\s+(.+?)$/s` consumed the first `- <hash>:` (used before #1271)          | 89       | v1.21.3, v1.17.2, v1.0.1          |\n| `CHANGELOG.md` has more list items than the release, e.g. two `## 1.48.1` version commits (`977129778`, `8ae1de446`) later merged into one section | 37       | v1.48.1, v1.46.8, v1.21.2         |\n| Only the first `### … Changes` section was kept (`(?=###\\|$)`), so a Minor release lost its Patch section, and so on        | 4        | v0.44.0, v0.46.0, v0.48.0, v1.4.0 |\n| Trailing quotes were stripped by `.replace(/(['\"])+$/g, '')`                                                                 | 3        | v1.20.1, v1.38.3, v1.49.3         |\n| A literal `\\n` in a code span became a line break (`.replace(/\\\\n/g, '\\n')`)                                                 | 2        | v0.51.12, v1.56.2                 |\n| The sanitizer masked code and option names (RC4)                                                                            | 2        | v2.33.5, v2.33.6                  |\n| The body differs in other ways (the CHANGELOG text was edited after the release)                                            | 4        | v1.0.1, v1.21.4, v1.22.5, v1.23.7 |\n\nA release can have several causes, so the counts add up to more than 102.\n`.replace(/---.*$/s, '')` (cut at the first `---`) is also in the old formatter.\nNo current CHANGELOG section has a `---` line inside it, but a changeset with a\nMarkdown rule would have been cut, so the new code and the tests cover it.\n\n### RC3 – Minor and Major releases were not formatted (37 releases)\n\nUntil #1271 the formatter matched only `### Patch Changes`. After #1271 it also\nmatched `### Minor Changes`, but never `### Major Changes`. When nothing matched\nit exited with \"Could not parse\" and the release kept the raw CHANGELOG text,\nwith no PR link and no npm badge (v0.39.0 … v1.22.0, and v2.0.0).\n\n### RC4 – the publication sanitizer masked code (v2.33.5, v2.33.6, plus four latent cases)\n\nThe release body goes through `sanitizeForPublication`. Its rules treated these\nas credentials:\n\n- `…Tokens: [REDACTED] and `token => [REDACTED] the value was `false` followed by a\n  closing backtick, or `…`.\n- `KNO…ARS`: the all-caps vendor-token pattern matched an\n  identifier without a digit.\n- `--tokens-budget-stats [REDACTED] and `--max-tokens [REDACTED] the CLI-credential rule\n  matched any `--…tokens…` option.\n- `…=<tokens>`: a placeholder was treated as a value.\n\nThe live releases contained only the first two cases. The repair dry run found\nthe other four (v0.54.4, v1.38.0, v1.58.0 and v1.64.3), and they would have been\npublished if the formatter had simply been fixed and rerun.\n\n## Fix everywhere in this repository\n\n| Place                                         | Change                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |\n| --------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| `scripts/format-release-notes.lib.mjs` (new)  | Pure functions. `buildReleaseDescription` keeps every `### Major/Minor/Patch Changes` section (headings are kept when there are several), keeps indentation, `---`, `\\n`, quotes and `- <hash>:` markers, and only strips trailing whitespace. Also: `extractChangelogSection`, `buildReleaseBody`, `findFormattingDefects`, `planReleaseRepair` and `formatChangelogListItem`. |\n| `scripts/format-release-notes.mjs`            | Uses the library. Adds a `--verbose` / `VERBOSE` mode that logs the sections, hashes and PRs found. The PR lookup (#1271/#1452) is unchanged.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |\n| `scripts/create-github-release.mjs`           | Uses `extractChangelogSection`, which needs the whole heading line `## <version>` (the old regex `## ${version}[\\s\\S]*?(?=## \\d\\|$)` let `2.3.1` match `## 2.3.10` and treated the dots as wildcards).                                                                                                                                                                                                               |\n| `scripts/instant-version-bump.mjs`            | A manual release description was written as `- ${description}`, so a multi-line description had the same structure bug in `CHANGELOG.md` itself. It now uses `formatChangelogListItem`, which matches `@changesets/changelog-git`.                                                                                                                                                                                             |\n| `src/credential-sanitization-core.lib.mjs`    | The four false positives above are fixed. Real credentials next to them (`--token [REDACTED] `--access-tokens [REDACTED] `--github-token=[REDACTED] `SYN…456`, `token: [REDACTED] are still masked.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |\n| `scripts/repair-release-notes.mjs` (new)      | Rebuilds published releases from `CHANGELOG.md` through the same library and sanitizer. Dry run by default; `--apply` PATCHes; `--backup-dir` saves every old body; `--tag` limits it to some releases.                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |\n\nOther `.map(line => line.trim())` calls in `src/` were checked. They parse\ncommand output, `.gitignore`-style files or Telegram text, not Markdown that is\npublished, so they were left as they are. `scripts/merge-changesets.mjs` and\n`scripts/create-manual-changeset.mjs` keep the description as written, and\nChangesets then indents it.\n\n## Audit of all releases\n\n`experiments/issue-3445-audit-releases.mjs` compares each release body with its\n`CHANGELOG.md` section, using `findFormattingDefects`:\n\n| Result (before)            | Releases |\n| -------------------------- | -------- |\n| correct                    | 225      |\n| lost indentation           | 302      |\n| missing text               | 102      |\n| unformatted (Minor, Major) | 37       |\n| other difference           | 6        |\n| no CHANGELOG section       | 302      |\n\n(A release can be both \"lost indentation\" and \"missing text\".) The six \"other\ndifference\" releases (v0.48.2, v0.50.2, v0.50.5, v0.50.8, v0.50.10 and v0.51.4)\ndiffer only in whitespace or a list marker, for example v0.50.2 had lost the `-`\nof its item.\n\nThe 302 releases from before v0.38.9 have no `CHANGELOG.md` section, so there is\nnothing to compare them with, and they were left unchanged.\n\n## Repair of the published releases\n\n<!-- repair-results -->\n\n## Existing tools and research\n\n- **Changesets** writes the CHANGELOG with `@changesets/changelog-git` or\n  `@changesets/changelog-github`. Both indent continuation lines by two spaces,\n  as quoted above.\n- **changesets/action** with `createGithubReleases: true` publishes the\n  CHANGELOG section unchanged. It uses a regex over `#` headings (it skips code\n  fences) to find the section, and ends it at the next heading of the same depth\n  ([`src/utils.ts`](https://github.com/changesets/action/blob/main/src/utils.ts)).\n  That is the approach `extractChangelogSection` now follows: whole heading\n  lines, and no rewriting of the content.\n- **semantic-release** (`@semantic-release/release-notes-generator`) and\n  **release-please** generate notes from Conventional Commit subjects, so they\n  avoid the problem by never reformatting user-written Markdown. Switching\n  release tools is out of scope. The useful lesson is the same: treat\n  CHANGELOG Markdown as opaque and only append to it.\n- **GitHub's generate-notes API** (`POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/releases/generate-notes`)\n  lists merged PRs. It could replace the PR lookup, but it does not use the\n  changeset text.\n- **CommonMark**: §5.2 (\"List items\") defines when a block stays inside a list\n  item. GitHub's `/markdown` API (GFM) was used to check the renders in\n  `render/`.\n\n## Upstream report\n\n`format-release-notes.mjs` came from\n[link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template](https://github.com/link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template).\nThe current template copy still has `.map((line) => line.trim())`, the `---`\ntruncation, `\\n` conversion, quote stripping, the first `- <hash>:` being\nconsumed, and a lookup of only the first hash. It was reported in\n[link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template#236](https://github.com/link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/issues/236).\nThe report includes a runnable reproduction, real broken output\n(link-foundation/start v0.13.0), a workaround and the suggested code. It also\nlists the repositories that carry a copy, so that they can be fixed from one\nplace:\n\n- link-foundation: command-stream, gh-load-issue, gh-load-pull-request,\n  glab-setup-git-identity, pdf-to-markdown, start, test-anywhere and\n  lino-objects-codec;\n- link-assistant: agent, meta-expression, web-capture and web-search.\n\n## Decisions and assumptions\n\n- **What \"nicely formatted\" means for v2.37.1.** One changeset is one list item\n  in `CHANGELOG.md`, and that is how GitHub renders the CHANGELOG. The release\n  now renders the same way: one bullet whose 19 paragraphs are indented inside\n  it. Splitting it into 19 bullets would make the release differ from the\n  CHANGELOG, and it would need the changeset to be rewritten.\n- **Source of truth.** Releases were rebuilt from the current `CHANGELOG.md`. So\n  where the CHANGELOG was edited after a release (for example the merged\n  `## 1.48.1` sections), the release now shows the current text.\n- **PR links** already present in a release were kept. A release without a PR\n  line (the unformatted ones) gets its PRs from its commit hashes, as the\n  formatter does.\n- Editing a release has no side effects here: no workflow is triggered by\n  `release` events. The original bodies are backed up in\n  `data/all-releases.json`.\n\n## How to reproduce and verify\n\n```bash\n# Regression tests (default suite)\nnode tests/issue-3445-release-notes-formatting.test.mjs\nnode tests/issue-3445-release-notes-not-masked.test.mjs\nnode tests/test-format-release-notes-1271.mjs\n\n# Audit any set of releases against CHANGELOG.md\ngh api repos/link-assistant/hive-mind/releases --paginate --jq '[.[] | {id, tag_name, published_at, body}]' | jq -s add > /tmp/releases.json\nnode experiments/issue-3445-audit-releases.mjs /tmp/releases.json > /tmp/audit.tsv\n\n# Plan a repair (dry run) and apply it\nnode scripts/repair-release-notes.mjs --verbose\nnode scripts/repair-release-notes.mjs --tag v2.37.1 --apply --backup-dir /tmp/release-backups\n```\n"

Its `getReleaseLine` is\n(`node_modules/@changesets/changelog-git/dist/index.mjs`):\n\n```js\nconst [firstLine, ...futureLines] = changeset.summary.split('\\n').map(l => l.trimEnd());\nlet returnVal = `- ${changeset.commit ? `${changeset.commit.slice(0, 7)}: ` : ''}${firstLine}`;\nif (futureLines.length > 0) returnVal += `\\n${futureLines.map(l => `  ${l}`).join('\\n')}`;\n```\n\nSo a changeset becomes **one** list item, and every later line is indented by\ntwo spaces. CommonMark keeps a later block inside the list item only when it is\nindented to the item's content column, which is two columns for `- `\n([CommonMark 0.31.2, §5.2 List items](https://spec.commonmark.org/0.31.2/#list-items):\n\"indenting subsequent lines of Ls by W + N spaces, is a list item with Bs as its\ncontents\"). Remove the indentation and the paragraph ends the list.\n\n`changesets/action` creates GitHub releases by copying the `CHANGELOG.md`\nsection unchanged (`createRelease` in\n[`src/run.ts`](https://github.com/changesets/action/blob/main/src/run.ts) uses\n`body: changelogEntry.content`). The structure is only lost because this\nrepository rewrites the body afterwards.\n\n## Root causes\n\n### RC1 – every line was trimmed (lost indentation, 302 releases, including v2.37.1)\n\n`format-release-notes.mjs` cleaned the description with:\n\n```js\n.split('\\n')\n.map(line => line.trim()) // Trim whitespace from each line\n.join('\\n')\n```\n\nThe comment describes the intent (\"normalize whitespace\"), but for Markdown the\nleading whitespace is structure. Each continuation paragraph and nested list\nitem lost its two spaces. GitHub then closed the list after the first paragraph,\nwhich is exactly what v2.37.1 shows (`render/v2.37.1-before.html`):\n\n| Render of v2.37.1                      | Before | After |\n| -------------------------------------- | ------ | ----- |\n| `<li>` elements                        | 1      | 1     |\n| `<p>` inside the list item             | 0      | 19    |\n| `<p>` after the list                   | 20     | 2     |\n\n(The two paragraphs after the list in the repaired body are the\n`**Related Pull Request:** #3390` line and the npm badge, as before.)\n\nWhy it became visible now: `validate-changeset.mjs` allows exactly one\nchangeset per PR. PR #3390 shipped many changes, so its changeset had 19\nparagraphs. Earlier releases had the same bug, but with one or two paragraphs it\nwas easy to miss.\n\n### RC2 – text was dropped (102 releases)\n\n`data/missing-text-causes.txt` classifies every release whose body misses words\nof its `CHANGELOG.md` section:\n\n| Cause                                                                                                                       | Releases | Examples                          |\n| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- | --------------------------------- |\n| The regex `/### Patch Changes\\s*\\n\\s*-\\s+([a-f0-9]+):\\s+(.+?)$/s` consumed the first `- <hash>:` (used before #1271)          | 89       | v1.21.3, v1.17.2, v1.0.1          |\n| `CHANGELOG.md` has more list items than the release, e.g. two `## 1.48.1` version commits (`977129778`, `8ae1de446`) later merged into one section | 37       | v1.48.1, v1.46.8, v1.21.2         |\n| Only the first `### … Changes` section was kept (`(?=###\\|$)`), so a Minor release lost its Patch section, and so on        | 4        | v0.44.0, v0.46.0, v0.48.0, v1.4.0 |\n| Trailing quotes were stripped by `.replace(/(['\"])+$/g, '')`                                                                 | 3        | v1.20.1, v1.38.3, v1.49.3         |\n| A literal `\\n` in a code span became a line break (`.replace(/\\\\n/g, '\\n')`)                                                 | 2        | v0.51.12, v1.56.2                 |\n| The sanitizer masked code and option names (RC4)                                                                            | 2        | v2.33.5, v2.33.6                  |\n| The body differs in other ways (the CHANGELOG text was edited after the release)                                            | 4        | v1.0.1, v1.21.4, v1.22.5, v1.23.7 |\n\nA release can have several causes, so the counts add up to more than 102.\n`.replace(/---.*$/s, '')` (cut at the first `---`) is also in the old formatter.\nNo current CHANGELOG section has a `---` line inside it, but a changeset with a\nMarkdown rule would have been cut, so the new code and the tests cover it.\n\n### RC3 – Minor and Major releases were not formatted (37 releases)\n\nUntil #1271 the formatter matched only `### Patch Changes`. After #1271 it also\nmatched `### Minor Changes`, but never `### Major Changes`. When nothing matched\nit exited with \"Could not parse\" and the release kept the raw CHANGELOG text,\nwith no PR link and no npm badge (v0.39.0 … v1.22.0, and v2.0.0).\n\n### RC4 – the publication sanitizer masked code (v2.33.5, v2.33.6, plus four latent cases)\n\nThe release body goes through `sanitizeForPublication`. Its rules treated these\nas credentials:\n\n- `…Tokens: [REDACTED] and `token => [REDACTED] the value was `false` followed by a\n  closing backtick, or `…`.\n- `KNO…ARS`: the all-caps vendor-token pattern matched an\n  identifier without a digit.\n- `--tokens-budget-stats [REDACTED] and `--max-tokens [REDACTED] the CLI-credential rule\n  matched any `--…tokens…` option.\n- `…=<tokens>`: a placeholder was treated as a value.\n\nThe live releases contained only the first two cases. The repair dry run found\nthe other four (v0.54.4, v1.38.0, v1.58.0 and v1.64.3), and they would have been\npublished if the formatter had simply been fixed and rerun.\n\n## Fix everywhere in this repository\n\n| Place                                         | Change                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |\n| --------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| `scripts/format-release-notes.lib.mjs` (new)  | Pure functions. `buildReleaseDescription` keeps every `### Major/Minor/Patch Changes` section (headings are kept when there are several), keeps indentation, `---`, `\\n`, quotes and `- <hash>:` markers, and only strips trailing whitespace. Both indent continuation lines by two spaces,\n  as quoted above.\n- **changesets/action** with `createGithubReleases: true` publishes the\n  CHANGELOG section unchanged. It uses a regex over `#` headings (it skips code\n  fences) to find the section, and ends it at the next heading of the same depth\n  ([`src/utils.ts`](https://github.com/changesets/action/blob/main/src/utils.ts)).\n  That is the approach `extractChangelogSection` now follows: whole heading\n  lines, and no rewriting of the content.\n- **semantic-release** (`@semantic-release/release-notes-generator`) and\n  **release-please** generate notes from Conventional Commit subjects, so they\n  avoid the problem by never reformatting user-written Markdown. Switching\n  release tools is out of scope. The useful lesson is the same: treat\n  CHANGELOG Markdown as opaque and only append to it.\n- **GitHub's generate-notes API** (`POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/releases/generate-notes`)\n  lists merged PRs. It could replace the PR lookup, but it does not use the\n  changeset text.\n- **CommonMark**: §5.2 (\"List items\") defines when a block stays inside a list\n  item. GitHub's `/markdown` API (GFM) was used to check the renders in\n  `render/`.\n\n## Upstream report\n\n`format-release-notes.mjs` came from\n[link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template](https://github.com/link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template).\nThe current template copy still has `.map((line) => line.trim())`, the `---`\ntruncation, `\\n` conversion, quote stripping, the first `- <hash>:` being\nconsumed, and a lookup of only the first hash. It was reported in\n[link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template#236](https://github.com/link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/issues/236).\nThe report includes a runnable reproduction, real broken output\n(link-foundation/start v0.13.0), a workaround and the suggested code. It also\nlists the repositories that carry a copy, so that they can be fixed from one\nplace:\n\n- link-foundation: command-stream, gh-load-issue, gh-load-pull-request,\n  glab-setup-git-identity, pdf-to-markdown, start, test-anywhere and\n  lino-objects-codec;\n- link-assistant: agent, meta-expression, web-capture and web-search.\n\n## Decisions and assumptions\n\n- **What \"nicely formatted\" means for v2.37.1.** One changeset is one list item\n  in `CHANGELOG.md`, and that is how GitHub renders the CHANGELOG. The release\n  now renders the same way: one bullet whose 19 paragraphs are indented inside\n  it. Splitting it into 19 bullets would make the release differ from the\n  CHANGELOG, and it would need the changeset to be rewritten.\n- **Source of truth.** Releases were rebuilt from the current `CHANGELOG.md`. So\n  where the CHANGELOG was edited after a release (for example the merged\n  `## 1.48.1` sections), the release now shows the current text.\n- **PR links** already present in a release were kept. A release without a PR\n  line (the unformatted ones) gets its PRs from its commit hashes, as the\n  formatter does.\n- Editing a release has no side effects here: no workflow is triggered by\n  `release` events. The original bodies are backed up in\n  `data/all-releases.json`.\n\n## How to reproduce and verify\n\n```bash\n# Regression tests (default suite)\nnode tests/issue-3445-release-notes-formatting.test.mjs\nnode tests/issue-3445-release-notes-not-masked.test.mjs\nnode tests/test-format-release-notes-1271.mjs\n\n# Audit any set of releases against CHANGELOG.md\ngh api repos/link-assistant/hive-mind/releases --paginate --jq '[.[] | {id, tag_name, published_at, body}]' | jq -s add > /tmp/releases.json\nnode experiments/issue-3445-audit-releases.mjs /tmp/releases.json > /tmp/audit.tsv\n\n# Plan a repair (dry run) and apply it\nnode scripts/repair-release-notes.mjs --verbose\nnode scripts/repair-release-notes.mjs --tag v2.37.1 --apply --backup-dir /tmp/release-backups\n```\n",

It also cut the notes at the\n *   first `---` or `###` anywhere in the text, rewrote a literal `\\n` inside a\n *   code span into a line break, stripped quotes the text ends with, and kept\n *   only one of the `### Minor Changes` / `### Patch Changes` sections.\n *\n *   These helpers keep the Markdown structure exactly as changesets wrote it:\n *   only trailing whitespace is removed, sections are found by headings at the\n *   start of a line, and only a footer this formatter generated is stripped.\n *\n * Uses only Node built-ins so it can be unit tested without the network.\n *\n * @see https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/issues/3445\n */\n\nexport const PACKAGE_NAME = '@link-assistant/hive-mind';\n\n// The section headings changesets writes, at the start of a line only. Older formatter versions\n * also dropped whole `### ... Changes` sections, cut the notes at the first\n * `---`, turned a literal `\\n` into a line break and stripped trailing quotes.\n *\n * @see https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/issues/3445\n */\n\nimport assert from 'node:assert/strict';\nimport { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';\n\nimport { buildPrLine, buildReleaseBody, buildReleaseDescription, extractChangelogSection, extractCommitHashes, extractPrNumbers, findFormattingDefects, formatChangelogListItem, hasGeneratedFooter, normalizeMarkdown, planReleaseRepair, stripGeneratedFooter } from '../scripts/format-release-notes.lib.mjs';\n\nconst MULTI_PARAGRAPH = ['### Patch Changes', '', '- 68f606a: First change (issue #2293).', '', '  Second change (issue #2303).', '', '  - nested bullet', '  - another nested bullet', '', '  Third change with `HIVE_MIND_X` and a literal `\\\\n` in code.'].join('\\n');\n\n// The formatter before issue #3445, reduced to its line handling.\nconst trimEveryLine = text =>\n  text\n    .split('\\n')\n    .map(line => line.trim())\n    .join('\\n');\n\n// --- 1. In `CHANGELOG.md` the same text is one list item. `scripts/format-release-notes.mjs` called `.trim()` on every line. That removed the two-space indentation `@changesets/changelog-git` gives the later lines of a changeset, so under CommonMark §5.2 those paragraphs and nested bullets fell out of the list item.\n\nAn audit of all 893 releases against `CHANGELOG.md` found the same bug in 302 releases (v0.38.9 to v2.37.1). It also found five more defects in the same pipeline:\n\n- text cut at the first `---` or `###`;\n- the first `- <hash>:` marker consumed by the old Patch-only regex;\n- a literal `\\n` turned into a line break;\n- trailing quotes stripped;\n- Minor and Major releases never formatted at all.\n\nThe publication sanitizer also masked option and identifier names, such as `--tokens-budget-stats` and `KNO…ARS`, in the v2.33.5 and v2.33.6 notes.\n\nThe full case study is in [`docs/case-studies/issue-3445/README.md`](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/issue-3445-7cd6fd7f1b0b/docs/case-studies/issue-3445/README.md). It covers the timeline, the requirements, root causes RC1–RC4, the audit, the repair, existing tools and research, and how to reproduce.\n\n## Changes\n\n| File | Change |\n| --- | --- |\n| `scripts/format-release-notes.lib.mjs` (new) | Pure helpers. They keep indentation and every `### Major/Minor/Patch Changes` section; find sections only by headings at the start of a line; strip only the footer this formatter adds; and expose `findFormattingDefects`, `planReleaseRepair` and `formatChangelogListItem`. The footer pattern has no nested quantifier, which fixes the CodeQL alert raised on this PR. |\n| `scripts/format-release-notes.mjs` | Uses the library. Adds `--verbose` / `VERBOSE`, which logs the sections, hashes and PRs found. |\n| `scripts/create-github-release.mjs` | Takes the section by the whole `## <version>` line, so `2.3.1` no longer matches `## 2.3.10`. |\n| `scripts/instant-version-bump.mjs` | Indents later lines of a multi-line manual description the way Changesets does, so `CHANGELOG.md` itself is correct. |\n| `src/credential-sanitization-core.lib.mjs` | Fixes the four false positives. Real credentials next to them are still masked. |\n| `scripts/repair-release-notes.mjs` (new) | Rebuilds published releases from `CHANGELOG.md`. It is a dry run by default; `--apply` updates the releases and `--backup-dir` saves the old bodies. |\n| `tests/issue-3445-*.test.mjs`, `tests/test-format-release-notes-1271.mjs` | Regression tests (see below). |\n| Dockerfiles, `src/formal-ai-version.lib.mjs`, two pin tests | formal-ai 0.353.8 → 0.354.0. The dependency freshness gate failed this PR's CI ([run 39019944968](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/actions/runs/39019944968)) because a new formal-ai version was published in the meantime. 0.354.0 has no `openssl-sys` in Cargo.lock and needs rust-version 1.99; its changes don't touch `/health`, `--version` or the server routes. |\n| `.changeset/release-notes-formatting-3445.md` | The one patch changeset. |\n\n## Repair of the published releases\n\nAll damaged releases were repaired with `scripts/repair-release-notes.mjs`. The logs are in [`docs/case-studies/issue-3445/repair/`](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/tree/issue-3445-7cd6fd7f1b0b/docs/case-studies/issue-3445/repair):\n\n- **Dry run against the backup:** 366 to repair:\n  - 221 lost indentation;\n  - 81 lost indentation and missing text;\n  - 21 missing text;\n  - 37 unformatted;\n  - 6 different from `CHANGELOG.md`.\n- **v2.37.1** was repaired first. Then the bulk `--apply` run checked 894 releases and repaired 365, with 0 failures.\n- **v2.38.0** was published with the old formatter while this PR was open, and was repaired separately.\n- **Verification dry run on the live releases:** 0 left to repair (592 correct, 302 with no CHANGELOG section, all from before v0.38.9).\n\nThe old bodies of all releases are backed up in `data/all-releases.json`.\n\nNote: until this PR is merged, any new release still goes through the old formatter. If one is published before the merge, run `node scripts/repair-release-notes.mjs --apply` once after merging.\n\nGitHub's render of v2.37.1 (`POST /markdown`, `gfm` mode):\n\n| Before | After |\n| --- | --- |\n| ![before](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/issue-3445-7cd6fd7f1b0b/docs/case-studies/issue-3445/render/v2.37.1-before.png?raw=true) | ![after](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/issue-3445-7cd6fd7f1b0b/docs/case-studies/issue-3445/render/v2.37.1-after.png?raw=true) |\n\n## Upstream report\n\nEvery copy of the formatter comes from the pipeline template. Before the repair: 302 lost indentation, 102 missing text, 37 unformatted, 6 other. After: 0 defects.\n2. `node tests/issue-3445-release-notes-formatting.test.mjs` runs the formatter's tests.\n   - It reproduces the old line-trimming formatter on the real v2.37.1 section, and checks that its output has the flattened structure.\n   - It checks that the new formatter keeps the section exactly.\n   - It covers several sections, Major releases, `---`/`###` inside the text, CRLF, idempotence, the repair plan, the `formatChangelogListItem` CHANGELOG writer, and a footer regex that stays linear on long runs of blank lines.\n3. `node tests/issue-3445-release-notes-not-masked.test.mjs` runs the sanitizer false-positive tests.\n\n## Tests\n\n- **Local:**\n  - Pass: `issue-3445-release-notes-formatting`, `issue-3445-release-notes-not-masked`, `test-format-release-notes-1271`, the release and sanitizer tests (`check-release-needed-2175`, `release-*`, `issue-2397-*`, `test-token-sanitization`, `test-credential-sanitization-2111`, `test-issue-2189-*`), `formal-ai-tool-parity-3279`, `test-issue-2187-current-dependency-pins`, `scripts/check-dependency-freshness.mjs`, `scripts/validate-changeset.mjs`, `npm run lint` and `npm run format:check`.\n  - Fail on both `main` and this branch under local Node 26 only: `deliberate-draft-restarts-ai-2312` and `test-merge-changesets-1452`. It keeps the structure exactly as `CHANGELOG.md` has it.\n- **Version lookup:** a version's section is found by the whole heading line, so `2.3.1` no longer picks up `2.3.10`.\n- **Manual releases** (`scripts/instant-version-bump.mjs`): a multi-line description is now indented in `CHANGELOG.md` the way Changesets does it.\n- **Sanitizer:** the four false positives are fixed. Real tokens next to them are still hidden.\n- **Debug output:** both scripts accept `--verbose`.\n- **Repair script** (`scripts/repair-release-notes.mjs`): rebuilds published releases from `CHANGELOG.md`. It only reports by default; `--apply` changes the releases.\n\n**Repair.** I fixed v2.37.1 first, then 365 releases in one run with no failures. v2.38.0 was published with the old formatter while this work was in progress, so I repaired it separately. Summary\n\nFixes #3445.\n\nThe [v2.37.1 release notes](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/releases/tag/v2.37.1) showed one bullet followed by 19 loose paragraphs. In `CHANGELOG.md` the same text is one list item. `scripts/format-release-notes.mjs` called `.trim()` on every line. That removed the two-space indentation `@changesets/changelog-git` gives the later lines of a changeset, so under CommonMark §5.2 those paragraphs and nested bullets fell out of the list item.\n\nAn audit of all 893 releases against `CHANGELOG.md` found the same bug in 302 releases (v0.38.9 to v2.37.1). It also found five more defects in the same pipeline:\n\n- text cut at the first `---` or `###`;\n- the first `- <hash>:` marker consumed by the old Patch-only regex;\n- a literal `\\n` turned into a line break;\n- trailing quotes stripped;\n- Minor and Major releases never formatted at all.\n\nThe publication sanitizer also masked option and identifier names, such as `--tokens-budget-stats` and `KNO…ARS`, in the v2.33.5 and v2.33.6 notes.\n\nThe full case study is in [`docs/case-studies/issue-3445/README.md`](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/issue-3445-7cd6fd7f1b0b/docs/case-studies/issue-3445/README.md). It covers the timeline, the requirements, root causes RC1–RC4, the audit, the repair, existing tools and research, and how to reproduce.\n\n## Changes\n\n| File | Change |\n| --- | --- |\n| `scripts/format-release-notes.lib.mjs` (new) | Pure helpers. They keep indentation and every `### Major/Minor/Patch Changes` section; find sections only by headings at the start of a line; strip only the footer this formatter adds; and expose `findFormattingDefects`, `planReleaseRepair` and `formatChangelogListItem`. The footer pattern has no nested quantifier, which fixes the CodeQL alert raised on this PR. |\n| `scripts/format-release-notes.mjs` | Uses the library. Adds `--verbose` / `VERBOSE`, which logs the sections, hashes and PRs found. |\n| `scripts/create-github-release.mjs` | Takes the section by the whole `## <version>` line, so `2.3.1` no longer matches `## 2.3.10`. |\n| `scripts/instant-version-bump.mjs` | Indents later lines of a multi-line manual description the way Changesets does, so `CHANGELOG.md` itself is correct. |\n| `src/credential-sanitization-core.lib.mjs` | Fixes the four false positives. Real credentials next to them are still masked. |\n| `scripts/repair-release-notes.mjs` (new) | Rebuilds published releases from `CHANGELOG.md`. It is a dry run by default; `--apply` updates the releases and `--backup-dir` saves the old bodies. |\n| `tests/issue-3445-*.test.mjs`, `tests/test-format-release-notes-1271.mjs` | Regression tests (see below). |\n| Dockerfiles, `src/formal-ai-version.lib.mjs`, two pin tests | formal-ai 0.353.8 → 0.354.0. The dependency freshness gate failed this PR's CI ([run 39019944968](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/actions/runs/39019944968)) because a new formal-ai version was published in the meantime. 0.354.0 has no `openssl-sys` in Cargo.lock and needs rust-version 1.99; its changes don't touch `/health`, `--version` or the server routes. |\n| `.changeset/release-notes-formatting-3445.md` | The one patch changeset. |\n\n## Repair of the published releases\n\nAll damaged releases were repaired with `scripts/repair-release-notes.mjs`. The logs are in [`docs/case-studies/issue-3445/repair/`](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/tree/issue-3445-7cd6fd7f1b0b/docs/case-studies/issue-3445/repair):\n\n- **Dry run against the backup:** 366 to repair:\n  - 221 lost indentation;\n  - 81 lost indentation and missing text;\n  - 21 missing text;\n  - 37 unformatted;\n  - 6 different from `CHANGELOG.md`.\n- **v2.37.1** was repaired first. Then the bulk `--apply` run checked 894 releases and repaired 365, with 0 failures.\n- **v2.38.0** was published with the old formatter while this PR was open, and was repaired separately.\n- **Verification dry run on the live releases:** 0 left to repair (592 correct, 302 with no CHANGELOG section, all from before v0.38.9).\n\nThe old bodies of all releases are backed up in `data/all-releases.json`.\n\nNote: until this PR is merged, any new release still goes through the old formatter. If one is published before the merge, run `node scripts/repair-release-notes.mjs --apply` once after merging.\n\nGitHub's render of v2.37.1 (`POST /markdown`, `gfm` mode):\n\n| Before | After |\n| --- | --- |\n| ![before](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/issue-3445-7cd6fd7f1b0b/docs/case-studies/issue-3445/render/v2.37.1-before.png?raw=true) | ![after](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/issue-3445-7cd6fd7f1b0b/docs/case-studies/issue-3445/render/v2.37.1-after.png?raw=true) |\n\n## Upstream report\n\nEvery copy of the formatter comes from the pipeline template. I filed the bug there, with a repro, a workaround and a suggested fix: https://github.com/link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/issues/236\n\n## How to reproduce\n\n1. Audit the live releases against `CHANGELOG.md`. Before the repair: 302 lost indentation, 102 missing text, 37 unformatted, 6 other. After: 0 defects.\n   ```bash\n   gh api repos/link-assistant/hive-mind/releases --paginate --jq '[.[] | {id, tag_name, published_at, body}]' | jq -s add > /tmp/releases.json\n   node experiments/issue-3445-audit-releases.mjs /tmp/releases.json > /tmp/audit.tsv\n   ```\n2. `node tests/issue-3445-release-notes-formatting.test.mjs` runs the formatter's tests.\n   - It reproduces the old line-trimming formatter on the real v2.37.1 section, and checks that its output has the flattened structure.\n   - It checks that the new formatter keeps the section exactly.\n   - It covers several sections, Major releases, `---`/`###` inside the text, CRLF, idempotence, the repair plan, the `formatChangelogListItem` CHANGELOG writer, and a footer regex that stays linear on long runs of blank lines.\n3. `node tests/issue-3445-release-notes-not-masked.test.mjs` runs the sanitizer false-positive tests.\n\n## Tests\n\n- **Local:**\n  - Pass: `issue-3445-release-notes-formatting`, `issue-3445-release-notes-not-masked`, `test-format-release-notes-1271`, the release and sanitizer tests (`check-release-needed-2175`, `release-*`, `issue-2397-*`, `test-token-sanitization`, `test-credential-sanitization-2111`, `test-issue-2189-*`), `formal-ai-tool-parity-3279`, `test-issue-2187-current-dependency-pins`, `scripts/check-dependency-freshness.mjs`, `scripts/validate-changeset.mjs`, `npm run lint` and `npm run format:check`.\n  - Fail on both `main` and this branch under local Node 26 only: `deliberate-draft-restarts-ai-2312` and `test-merge-changesets-1452`. This PR doesn't cause them.\n  - The full local suite was stopped by the session's time limit at 246 of 671 test files.\n- **CI:** \"Checks and release\" [run 39021165357](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/actions/runs/39021165357) passes on 2ba255339, including test-suites and the dependency freshness gate. It also found five more defects in the same pipeline:\n\n- text cut at the first `---` or `###`;\n- the first `- <hash>:` marker consumed by the old Patch-only regex;\n- a literal `\\n` turned into a line break;\n- trailing quotes stripped;\n- Minor and Major releases never formatted at all.\n\nThe publication sanitizer also masked option and identifier names, such as `--tokens-budget-stats` and `KNO…ARS`, in the v2.33.5 and v2.33.6 notes.\n\nThe full case study is in [`docs/case-studies/issue-3445/README.md`](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/issue-3445-7cd6fd7f1b0b/docs/case-studies/issue-3445/README.md). It covers the timeline, the requirements, root causes RC1–RC4, the audit, the repair, existing tools and research, and how to reproduce.\n\n## Changes\n\n| File | Change |\n| --- | --- |\n| `scripts/format-release-notes.lib.mjs` (new) | Pure helpers. They keep indentation and every `### Major/Minor/Patch Changes` section; find sections only by headings at the start of a line; strip only the footer this formatter adds; and expose `findFormattingDefects`, `planReleaseRepair` and `formatChangelogListItem`. The footer pattern has no nested quantifier, which fixes the CodeQL alert raised on this PR. |\n| `scripts/format-release-notes.mjs` | Uses the library. Adds `--verbose` / `VERBOSE`, which logs the sections, hashes and PRs found. |\n| `scripts/create-github-release.mjs` | Takes the section by the whole `## <version>` line, so `2.3.1` no longer matches `## 2.3.10`. |\n| `scripts/instant-version-bump.mjs` | Indents later lines of a multi-line manual description the way Changesets does, so `CHANGELOG.md` itself is correct. |\n| `src/credential-sanitization-core.lib.mjs` | Fixes the four false positives. Real credentials next to them are still masked. |\n| `scripts/repair-release-notes.mjs` (new) | Rebuilds published releases from `CHANGELOG.md`. It is a dry run by default; `--apply` updates the releases and `--backup-dir` saves the old bodies. |\n| `tests/issue-3445-*.test.mjs`, `tests/test-format-release-notes-1271.mjs` | Regression tests (see below). |\n| Dockerfiles, `src/formal-ai-version.lib.mjs`, two pin tests | formal-ai 0.353.8 → 0.354.0. The dependency freshness gate failed this PR's CI ([run 39019944968](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/actions/runs/39019944968)) because a new formal-ai version was published in the meantime. 0.354.0 has no `openssl-sys` in Cargo.lock and needs rust-version 1.99; its changes don't touch `/health`, `--version` or the server routes. |\n| `.changeset/release-notes-formatting-3445.md` | The one patch changeset. |\n\n## Repair of the published releases\n\nAll damaged releases were repaired with `scripts/repair-release-notes.mjs`.
